The orthorhombic crystal Ba2Mg28Ti2 (reduced formula BaMg14Ti) adopts space group Amm2 (No. 38) with 32 atoms in the unit cell distributed over 9 independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis identifies close-packed-like local arrangements for Ba, Mg, and Ti centers, each with 12 geometric neighbors. Mg environments range from 2 Ba/4 Mg/6 Ti to 6 Ba/6 Mg, with Mg–Mg distances of roughly 3.23–3.39 Å. The periodic neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all 32 sites. Validated polyhedron contacts show Mg-centered 12-vertex coordination polyhedra sharing corners, edges, and faces.
